modules.module_title: Historical and Geographical Context of Kota Doria

pcs.pc_description: Describe the historical origins by identifying roots in Kota, Rajasthan, and outlining the evolution of the weaving tradition over time.
Explain the cultural importance by highlighting its royal associations and its continued role in traditional regional attire.
Identify the Hadoti region Kota, Bundi, and Baran as the primary production area, linking geographical setting to craft development.
Explain how the migration of weaving communities and support from royal households contributed to the refinement and preservation of the techniques.
Explore how local climate, geography, and customs influenced patterns, texture, and overall weaving style.

modules.module_title: Identify the Key Characteristics of Kota Doria Fabric

pcs.pc_description: Define the term “Doria” and identify the hallmark of the fabric, the small square checks woven into it, commonly known as “Kota khat” or “Kota Doria checks.”
Outline the traditional use of cotton yarns and explain how contemporary variations blend silk and synthetics to enhance strength and sheen.
Describe the integration of Zari (gold or silver thread) into both heritage and modern versions, contributing to the fabric’s decorative elegance.
Explain the fabric’s lightweight and sheer nature, created by the use of fine yarns and an open weave, making it ideal for hot and humid climates.
Recognise the adaptability of the fabric in producing sarees, dupattas, and scarves, and describe how design methods like block printing and tie-and-dye complement its texture.

modules.module_title: Recognise the Role of Artisans in Kota Doria Weaving

pcs.pc_description: Describe the integral role of skilled artisans, or karigars, in the creation process, highlighting their expertise in producing the signature weave.
Understand the traditional techniques employed on handlooms, including shuttle weaving, and how such methods are preserved through generational practice.
Recognise hand-weaving as a sustainable, labour-intensive process that reflects the cultural richness of rural Rajasthan.
Appreciate the craftsmanship and precision required to produce intricate design and patterns unique to this heritage fabric.
Acknowledge the collective effort of local weaving communities in safeguarding the identity and continuity of this craft tradition.

modules.module_title: Understand the Significance of Kota Doria in Modern Fashion and Culture

pcs.pc_description: Examine the fabric’s continued relevance in modern fashion by identifying its use in garments such as sarees, kurtas, and dupattas, and outline its evolution from traditional to contemporary styles.
Explore the cultural and commercial value of Kota Doria by assessing its market presence in India and abroad, and explain how the GI mark supports authenticity and protects the craft from imitation.
Recognise the craft’s contribution to the local economy by outlining how handloom weaving sustains livelihoods and drives income for artisan communities in the Hadoti region.
Discuss the growing demand for variations such as embroidered, printed, and embellished designs, and explain how these innovations help promote traditional skills in evolving markets.
Appreciate the integration of handwoven fabric into both high fashion and everyday clothing, and describe its role in sustainability and preserving craft heritage through conscious consumer trends.

modules.module_title: Design Conceptualisation and Translation

pcs.pc_description: Translate customer designs onto graph paper, ensuring accuracy for weaving.
Prepare the loom according to design specifications, including warp yarn selection.
Select appropriate colours, considering traditional and contemporary preferences.
Incorporate Zari threads into the weave to enhance the fabric's richness.

modules.module_title: Inspect and Maintain Loom Components

pcs.pc_description: Examine the loom thoroughly for signs of wear, misalignment, or damage prior to use, ensuring safe and efficient operation.
Clean key components -reed, heddles, shafts, beams and removing accumulated dust, lint, and old yarn residues.
Use soft brushes or cloth to eliminate debris that may hinder weaving quality or machine movement.

modules.module_title: Prepare the Warp and Beam the Loom

Draw warp threads accurately through lease rods, heddles, and the reed according to the threading plan.
Maintain even spacing and uniform tension across the warp to avoid weaving defects.
Securely tie warp ends to the cloth beam using standard knotting techniques suitable for Kota Doria weaving.
Adjust the brake and tensioning devices to maintain consistent warp tension during production.

pcs.pc_description: Select shuttles appropriate to the type and thickness of the weft yarn in use.
Wind weft yarn onto bobbins or pirns using manual or mechanical winding tools with care to prevent tangling.
Insert the bobbin into the shuttle and test its smooth movement through the shed.
Confirm that the shuttle race and picker mechanism function without obstruction or misfire.
Make necessary adjustments to shuttle boxes or picker arms to ensure uniform weft placement and alignment.

GS8. Work cooperatively with fellow artisans to ensure a fair and safe work environment.
GS9. Share sustainable ideas or techniques with peers to encourage best practices.
GS10. Keep simple records of material usage and waste reduction.
GS11. Participate in discussions about community involvement and cultural preservation.
GS12. Support fair trade and ethical practices in marketing woven products.
GS13. Observe and report areas where weaving practices could be made more sustainable.
GS14. Take initiative to improve one's knowledge of eco-friendly tools and techniques.
GS15. Maintain a positive attitude towards learning and applying sustainable innovations.

modules.module_title: Understand Sustainability Principles in Handloom Weaving

pcs.pc_description: Describe the concept of sustainability and its importance in preserving traditional weaving crafts.
Explain environmental, economic, and social aspects of sustainability specific to Kota Doria weaving.
Identify the impact of weaving practices on natural resources and local communities.

modules.module_title: Promote Sustainable Material Selection and Usage

pcs.pc_description: Select eco-friendly raw materials such as organic cotton and natural dyes suitable for Kota Doria weaving.
Assess suppliers for sustainable sourcing practices and ethical labour conditions.
Minimise material waste during yarn preparation and weaving by careful planning and resource management.

modules.module_title: Implement Sustainable Weaving Techniques and Processes

pcs.pc_description: Use energy-efficient handloom techniques that reduce reliance on electricity or harmful machinery.
Apply water-efficient methods for dyeing and finishing to reduce environmental impact.
Encourage reuse and recycling of leftover yarns and fabric scraps within the production cycle.

modules.module_title: Segregation and safe disposal of weaving Waste

pcs.pc_description: Identify and categorise all types of weaving waste such as yarn ends, thread cuttings, fabric rejects, and packaging material.
Follow standard procedures for segregating waste into recyclable, non-recyclable, and hazardous categories.
Ensure proper labelling and storage of segregated waste in designated containers or bins.
Adhere to environmentally safe methods for disposing of non-recyclable waste in line with regulations.
Avoid mixing different types of waste to prevent contamination and facilitate easy recycling.

modules.module_title: Foster Social and Economic Sustainability

pcs.pc_description: Support fair wages, safe working conditions, and skill development for weaving artisans.
Engage local communities in decision- making processes to preserve cultural heritage.
Promote market strategies that highlight the sustainable and ethical values of Kota Doria products.

modules.module_title: Monitor, Evaluate, and Improve Sustainability Practices

pcs.pc_description: Establish procedures to regularly monitor environmental and social impacts of weaving operations.
Document and analyse sustainability performance data to identify areas for improvement.
Implement corrective actions and innovative practices to enhance sustainability outcomes continuously.
